Flag careless real respondents

Source: R/behaviour.R
flag_careless.Rd

Experimental. flag_careless() marks real respondents whose answers look careless, using the eight behaviour_features(). By default a respondent is careless when at least two features fall in the real data's most extreme 2.5% on the careless side: The highest 2.5% for extreme, midpoint, acquiescence, key_inconsistency and mahalanobis, the lowest 2.5% for even_odd and person_fit, and the lowest or highest 1.25% for variability. These are the flags behind clean_real = TRUE in synthetic_behaviour() and authenticity_benchmark().

Usage

flag_careless(real, items, rule = NULL, fit_scales = NULL)

Arguments

real

a data frame of real responses.

items

a data frame with one row per item: item (column name), scale (or trait, as in hexaco_items), an optional facet and an optional logical reverse.

rule

optional function that takes the tibble of features (one row per respondent) and returns a logical vector, TRUE for careless respondents. It replaces the default rule.

fit_scales

the scales used for person fit. NULL uses all scales; character(0) skips person fit (the person_fit column is then NA).

Value

A tibble with one row per respondent of real: row (the row in real), the eight features, n_flags (the number of features in the careless 2.5%, or NA with a user rule) and careless.

See also

behaviour_features(), synthetic_behaviour()

Examples

h <- hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ]
real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
fl <- flag_careless(real, h, fit_scales = character(0))
mean(fl$careless)
#> [1] 0.03337237
